title: Interphase to cytokinesis: the stages of mitosis
examples: What are the stages of mitosis?
Why do cells copy their DNA before dividing?

explain.say: When you graze your knee, new skin grows back in a few days. Where do all those new cells come from? Each one is made when an old cell splits in two, in a careful dance called mitosis. Let's follow it round.

explain.say: Start at the top: interphase. This is the busy time before dividing. The cell grows and makes an exact copy of all its DNA. Why do you think it needs two full copies?

explain.say: Next is anaphase. Thin fibres pull each chromosome apart, one copy to each end of the cell. So each end gets the very same set. What would go wrong if one end got too few?

faq.a: In interphase the cell grows, makes more organelles such as mitochondria and ribosomes, and copies its DNA so each chromosome becomes two identical strands joined in the middle.
In metaphase the chromosomes line up along the middle of the cell. Spindle fibres attach to each one, ready to pull the two copies apart.
In anaphase the spindle fibres shorten and pull the two copies of each chromosome to opposite ends of the cell, so each end gets a complete set.
Cytokinesis is the final split. The cytoplasm and cell membrane divide to make two separate daughter cells, each with its own nucleus. In plants a new cell wall forms between them.
Mitosis makes genetically identical cells for growth, for repairing damage like a cut, and for asexual reproduction in some plants and animals.

facts: The stages of mitosis are prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase, followed by cytokinesis.
Mitosis produces two daughter cells that are genetically identical to the parent cell.

quiz.say: In which stage do chromosomes line up across the middle of the cell?

quiz.why: In metaphase the chromosomes line up on the cell's equator.

wrong.1: In anaphase they are being pulled apart to the ends.
wrong.2: In interphase the DNA is long and thin and copying itself, not lined up.

quiz.say: Why must DNA be copied before mitosis?
quiz.show: Why must DNA be copied before mitosis?

options.show: So each new cell gets a full set
options.say: So each new cell gets a full set

quiz.why: Copying DNA first means each of the two new cells gets a complete, identical set of chromosomes.

wrong.1: The purpose is complete instructions, not weight.
wrong.2: Mitosis makes identical cells, not different ones.
